verdict.rationale: Hoppscotch's own CLI docs say it can run collection tests and 'manage automated API monitoring' from a terminal or an automated system, and it can emit JUnit reports for collection runs. However, nothing documents built-in scheduling or alerting, so recurring runs and failure alerts appear to depend on external cron/CI tooling. Missing for 10: native scheduled monitor runs, built-in alerting/notifications on failure, detailed monitoring docs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can schedule collection runs as monitors that alert me when an API breaks

citations.quote: With the command-line interface (CLI) you can interact with the Hoppscotch platform using a terminal, or through an automated system. This enables you to run API tests, manage automated API monitoring
Use the Hoppscotch CLI to run API tests, automate monitoring, and manage collections from your terminal.
The hopp test command now has the ability to generate a JUnit Report for collection runs in the CLI.
